newsitem.title: UK: Dollar orbits 1.83 marks in Europe, eyes on Buba.
newsitem.headline: Dollar orbits 1.83 marks in Europe, eyes on Buba.

text.p: The dollar was firm against the mark at midday in Europe, orbiting the 1.83 level ahead of the outcome of today's Bundesbank council meeting, its last before the summer recess.
Dealers said trade was fairly quiet with the market wary of any mark-positive statements from German central bank members. The Bundesbank said there would be no post-meeting news briefing.

"I don't think we'll see much today. The U.S., UK and Germany have had plenty of occasion over the last week to cap the buoyant market but they didn't," said Claudio Demolli, foreign exchange analyst at Merrill Lynch in London.
The only risk for the current mark downtrend is a change in German monetary policy but Demolli saw the Bundesbank being comfortable with German inflation at current levels.
Speculation that the Bundesbank might switch to a variable repo at today's meeting has been circulating but analysts were largely dismissive of this prospect going into the summer break.

Dealers said a switch to a variable repo rate would send a strong signal to the market and might serve to put a floor on mark weakness but so far the German authorities have appeared relatively tolerant of the recent dollar gains.
By 1100 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.8294/99 marks, down from an overnight high of 1.8315 but still above late Wednesday's 1.8240/50 marks.
There was little reaction to earlier comments on German radio from German 'wise-man' Rolf Peffekoven that he did not expect the dollar to climb higher from current levels.
Peffekoven, one of Germany's council of independent economic adivsers, also said G7 could intervene to halt dollar gains.
"This seemed more likely around 1.80 marks but now people are thinking levels around 1.85 is where authorities will start getting nervous," said a UK bank dealer.
A decline in mark/yen by the European midsession from its overnight and early European highs provided some dollar/mark support, though it also saw dollar/yen edge down from its session highs.
Mark/yen slumped to 63.09/12 from an earlier peak of 63.57 and late Wednesday's 63.47/49.
Dollar/yen stood at 115.67/77, down from a session top of 115.92 and 115.73/78 late Wednesday.
